title: Stable bibliographic identity and canon-citation scheme for citing the trilogy's volumes and passages
question: Which bibliographic identifiers, metadata standards and deposit rules actually govern a German-language YA trilogy and establish how its official website should cite individual volumes and passages so citations survive edition changes — ISBN-13/GTIN under ISO 2108 and the German ISBN agency, ONIX 3.0 trade metadata, registration in the Deutsche Nationalbibliografie and DNB legal deposit, schema.org Book/BookSeries markup, and DOI/Crossref registration for books where a publisher assigns one — and what do those standards require of a citation scheme that maps an explainer page to a specific canon passage rather than to an informal Band/Kapitel reference?
why_now: README.md defines the project as the website of the Endia trilogy, but no content or citation convention exists yet; every future explainer page will need a stable target, and changing identifiers after pages are written means rewriting the whole canon-to-evidence map. The repository is still at initial-structure stage, so the convention is cheap to fix now.
real_world_anchor: Bibliographic metadata standards (ISO 2108, ONIX 3.0, schema.org Book/BookSeries), German legal deposit and national-bibliography practice, and persistent identifier schemes for books.
novelty_reason: No queued topic addresses how the books themselves are identified and cited. RES-20261015-00F9F49D covers quotation rights in the novels' text and cover art, not bibliographic identity, edition tracking or a stable canon-citation scheme.
